module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 6

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/6](https://www.erdosproblems.com/6)
- [BFT15] Banks, William D. and Freiberg, Tristan and Turnage-Butterbaugh, Caroline L., Consecutive primes in tuples. Acta Arith. (2015), 261-266.
- [Ma15] Maynard, James, Small gaps between primes. Ann. of Math. (2) (2015), 383-413.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos6

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < d_{n+2}$, where $d$
denotes the prime gap function.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6 :
    {n | primeGap n < primeGap (n + 1) ∧ primeGap (n + 1) < primeGap (n + 2)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < \dots < d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6.variants.increasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) < primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry


/--
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n > d_{n+1} \dots > d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6.variants.decreasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) > primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos6

reformulations.difference: BFT15 Corollary 1 counts the number L ≥ 2 of gaps in a run. Lean instead quantifies over m : ℕ and requires m adjacent comparisons, describing m+1 gaps.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For m ≥ 1 set L=m+1; conversely, for L ≥ 2 set m=L−1. Adjacent strict inequalities are equivalent to strict monotonicity of the run indexed by Fin (m+1). The extra m=0 case has no comparisons and its starting-index set is all of ℕ, hence infinite. The equivalence of the universally quantified formulations was proved in scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: BFT15 Corollary 1 counts L ≥ 2 gaps, whereas Lean counts m adjacent comparisons and permits m=0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The substitution L=m+1 identifies all nontrivial cases. The adjacent decreasing comparisons are equivalent to strict antitonicity on Fin (m+1). The additional m=0 case simply asserts infinitude of ℕ. The equivalence of the universally quantified formulations was proved in scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh, Consecutive primes in tuples, Corollary 1 and its proof: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.7003 ; LaTeX source read at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1311.7003 .
Maynard, Small gaps between primes, introduction and Propositions 4.2–4.3: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.4600 ; LaTeX source read at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1311.4600 .
Local Mathlib sources: Data/Nat/Nth.lean, Data/Nat/Prime/Nth.lean, Data/Finset/Range.lean, and Order/Fin/Basic.lean.
review.notes: All three declarations agree with BFT15 Corollary 1; the main theorem is its three-gap increasing case. Their research solved tags are supported by that paper. Lean checks confirmed positive, genuinely consecutive-prime gaps, harmless zero-based indexing, the m=0 and m=1 boundaries, and that m=2 matches the main conjunction. Explicit increasing and decreasing examples and the indexing/length equivalences compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry dependencies. Access limitation: erdosproblems.com/6 returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its live wording and metadata could not be read. Mathematical verification used the cited primary papers instead.
